product.reading: Reading what fires and who is on call.

contactHints.slack: An incoming webhook of a Slack app: https://hooks.slack.com/services/…
contactHints.teams: A Teams workflow that posts a card it is sent to a channel.
contactHints.webhook: Any address: it gets the whole group as JSON, for a phone or SMS provider among others.

overviewPage.description: What fires now, who is on call and what was sent.
overviewPage.failed_one: {{count}} notification did not get through in the last day
overviewPage.failed_other: {{count}} notifications did not get through in the last day
overviewPage.failedDetail: Nobody was told of those alerts. Check the contact point: its webhook may have been removed.
overviewPage.unrouted_one: {{count}} group fires that no route takes
overviewPage.unrouted_other: {{count}} groups fire that no route takes
overviewPage.unroutedDetail: Nobody is told of them. Add a route with no matchers last, to take everything left.
overviewPage.quietDetail: When Prometheus or a product sends an alert, it shows here.
overviewPage.perHourDetail: The last 24 hours, tests left out.

welcomePage.description: Alerts takes alerts from Prometheus, products and scripts, groups those of one problem, and tells whoever is on call.
welcomePage.step1: Add a contact point under Routing: a Slack or Teams channel, or any webhook.
welcomePage.step2: Add a route that sends to it. A route with no matchers takes every alert.
welcomePage.step3: Under On-call, make a schedule, so each notification names who is on call.
welcomePage.step4: Point Prometheus at Alerts as its Alertmanager, or send alerts from a script. See Setup.
welcomePage.alreadyFiring_one: {{count}} alert fires already, and nobody is told until a route takes it
welcomePage.alreadyFiring_other: {{count}} alerts fire already, and nobody is told until a route takes them

groupsPage.description: Alerts of one problem, as people are told about them: grouped by the route's labels.

groupPage.notFoundDetail: Its alerts resolved over an hour ago, or it never existed.
groupPage.unrouted: No route takes these alerts, so nobody is told.
groupPage.ackedDetail: No repeats and no escalation until a new alert joins the group.
groupPage.noNotificationsDetail: A group is told of after the group wait, 30 seconds unless set otherwise.

silencesPage.description: Maintenance windows. A silence stops notifications, never the alerts: they stay on the screens.
silencesPage.newDetail: Alerts whose labels match every matcher are silenced.

oncallPage.description: Who is on call: members take turns, and notifications name the person on call.
oncallPage.name: Name
oncallPage.membersHint: One per line. After a comma, a Slack user id such as U024BE7LH mentions them in Slack.
oncallPage.noneDetail: Make one so notifications say who is on call.
oncallPage.notStarted: Its first shift has not started.

routingPage.description: Where notifications go. Routes are tried in order; the first whose matchers all match takes the alert.
routingPage.contactPointsDetail: Their addresses are kept sealed and never shown again in full. Only admins add or delete them.
routingPage.name: Name
routingPage.noContactsDetail: Add a Slack or Teams channel, or a webhook.
routingPage.routesDetail: Group by the labels of one problem, such as alertname and cluster. Repeat until someone acknowledges; escalate when nobody does.
routingPage.noRoutes: No routes: nobody is told of anything.

historyPage.description: Every notification sent, newest first, and whether it got through.

setupPage.description: How alerts reach Alerts. Each needs ALERTS_INGEST_TOKEN, or an API token with the editor role.
setupPage.prometheusDetail: Your alerting rules stay where they are: Alerts takes their alerts as an Alertmanager would.
setupPage.scriptDetail: Send the alert again while it holds; it resolves after five minutes without one, or at its endsAt.
setupPage.alertmanagerDetail: Its webhook works too, with the status of each alert.

settingsPage.askAnAdmin: Ask an admin of this alerts.

account.title: Account
account.description: Your profile, password, two-step verification and where you are signed in.

members.title: Members
members.description: Who can sign in to this alerts, and with which role. Viewers see everything; editors also acknowledge, silence, keep schedules and test contact points; admins also add contact points and change routes, and manage members and tokens.

signin.title: Sign-in
signin.description: Identity providers people can sign in with, such as OpenAsy Identity, Keycloak or Microsoft Entra ID, and which of their groups give which role.

tokens.title: API tokens
tokens.description: For scripts and CI. Each token has one role and an expiry; the secret is shown once.
